title: Fact admission — reference cases
nature: Synthetic data. Fictional organisations and messages. Expected outcomes and reasons are human-defined.

outcomes.ADMIT: admit as proposed, with the stated attribution and evidence class
outcomes.ADMIT-QUALIFIED: admit only as a weaker proposition or an evidence-only note
outcomes.HOLD: do not admit yet; a specific question or confirmation is needed
outcomes.REFUSE: do not admit; the stated reason applies

reasons.subject_ambiguous: HOLD: the subject matches more than one organisation; ask which
reasons.quote_not_in_source: REFUSE: the quoted text does not occur in the cited material
reasons.period_missing: HOLD: a rate with no stated period cannot fill a measurement field; ask which period
reasons.not_entitled_to_commit: REFUSE: the submitting account is not entitled to commit the company
reasons.stronger_than_source: ADMIT-QUALIFIED: the source supports only a weaker, conditional proposition
reasons.confirmations_pending: HOLD: not every party the change binds has confirmed it
reasons.as_subject_transcription: ADMIT: as the subject's own transcription, at that assurance level
reasons.assurance_claimed_for_other_party: REFUSE: assurance is claimed on behalf of another party
reasons.independent_issuer: ADMIT: issued by an independent party with standing
reasons.field_not_declared: REFUSE: the record carries a field the target contract does not declare

reasonVocabulary: Reasons are this file's own descriptive labels, not Tinor's internal vocabulary. Outputs scored against this file must use one of them, or null.
stages: stopsAt names one of six high-level stages: Interpretation, Typed Candidate, Assessment, Human Confirmation and authority, Owner Commit / Durable Record, Read.

tinorCoverageValues.tested: Tinor's own automated tests exercise the corresponding behaviour (Tinor's claim; nothing in this folder checks it)
tinorCoverageValues.integration-test: covered by a Tinor test that needs a database
tinorCoverageValues.design: described in Tinor's design records; no test cited

cases.title: Same name, two organisations
cases.input: Email signature: 'Northfield — Sales'. Body: 'Our HX-40 lead time is now six weeks.'
cases.context: Two registered organisations are named Northfield: org:northfield-components (the buyer's supplier) and org:northfield-precision. The model bound the email to the second because its directory entry was the closer text match.
cases.why: A name match is not evidence of identity. The candidate cannot be bound until a person chooses the entity; nothing is admitted against either organisation in the meantime.

cases.title: The quote is not in the document
cases.input: Supplier upload: resin test report PDF for grade PC-ABS 2200. Model summary: 'The report shows PC-ABS 2400 meets UL 94 V-0 at 1.5 mm.'
cases.context: The cited material is a report on a different grade. The quoted span does not occur in it.
cases.why: A candidate must point to text that exists in the material on record. A plausible summary of a neighbouring document is not grounding.

cases.title: A rate hidden in the unit
cases.context: The capacity target requires a count over an explicit interval. 'Per month' names no month.
cases.why: The value may be right, but the field cannot hold it without knowing which month and on what basis. The remedy is a question, not a refusal of the supplier.

cases.title: A commitment from an account that cannot commit
cases.input: Email from a sales coordinator: 'Confirmed: 20,000 HX-40 housings delivered by 30 November at USD 1.85.'
cases.context: The coordinator's account may submit records but is not authorised to commit Northfield Components.
cases.why: Being able to call the write API is not authority to bind the company. Permission to submit records is not permission to commit on the company's behalf.

cases.title: A hedge promoted to a promise
cases.input: Email from Northfield's sales director: 'We should be able to ship the 20,000 housings by end of November, assuming the resin arrives on time.'
cases.context: The sender has authority to commit, but the sentence is conditional and hedged. The model dropped both the condition and 'should be able to'.
cases.why: What the source supports is a dated, attributed expectation with its condition attached: an evidence-only note. Recording it as a delivery commitment would create an obligation nobody made.

cases.title: A firm quote that is not yet an agreement
cases.input: Email from Northfield's sales director: 'We offer 20,000 HX-40 housings, delivery by 30 November 2026, USD 1.85 per unit, valid until 31 October.'
cases.context: The sender may commit for Northfield. The buyer has not confirmed. The proposer listed only itself as a required confirmer.
cases.why: An offer becomes shared state only when every party the change affects confirms the same change set. The required set is derived from the change, so the proposer cannot shrink it.

cases.title: An honest self-declared transcription
cases.input: Supplier record: 'Flammability test report FR-118 for PC-ABS 2200, issued by Lakeside Labs, result V-0 at 1.5 mm.' Recorded by the supplier, marked as its own transcription.
cases.context: The supplier claims nothing more than that it transcribed the report it holds.
cases.why: A self-declared claim is valid when it says what it is. It is admitted as the supplier's transcription, at that assurance level and no higher.

cases.title: The supplier writes the lab's attestation
cases.input: Same report, but the supplier's event marks it 'attested by Lakeside Labs' and names the lab as assessor.
cases.context: The event is signed by the supplier's account, not the lab's.
cases.why: Only the lab can attest as the lab. A supplier claiming third-party assurance on the lab's behalf is refused rather than admitted at a lower level.

cases.title: The lab issues its own report
cases.input: Lakeside Labs records report FR-118 under its own account, naming itself as assessor.
cases.context: The issuing account is the lab's and is independent of the supplier.
cases.why: The same content is admissible at a higher assurance level when the party with standing issues it.

cases.title: An extra field claims verification
cases.input: An integration posts the supplier's lead-time record with an added field "verified": true.
cases.context: The target contract does not declare a 'verified' field.
cases.why: Assurance is derived from who issued what, not from a flag in the payload. Undeclared fields are refused, not ignored.
